The season began on 4 February and was scheduled to end on 13 November 2022.{{cite web |url=https://www.la-razon.com/marcas/2021/12/21/confirmado-tres-torneos-para-el-2022/|title=Confirmado: tres their value in the quarter-finals and semi-finals|language=es|publisher=Página Siete|date=18 May 2022|access-date=2 June 2022}} In the Torneo Apertura, [[Club Bolívar|Bolívar]] won their thirtieth league title and twenty-fourth in the professional era, by defeating crosstown rivals [[The Strongest]] in the final match played on 12 June by a 3–0 score.{{cite web |url=https://premiumsportsbo.com/bolivar-madruga-al-tigre-y-es-indiscutible-monarca/|title=Bolívar 'madruga' al Tigre y es monarca indiscutible|trans-title=Bolívar hits the ''Tiger'' early and is undisputed monarch|language=es|publisher=Premium|date=12 June 2022|access-date=12 June 2022}} On the other hand, the Torneo Clausura was abandoned on 10 November 2022 with 24 out of 30 rounds played and no champion was declared due to civil unrest in the [[Santa Cruz Department (Bolivia)|Santa Cruz Department]].{{cite web|url=https://www.lostiempos.com/deportes/futbol/20221110/consejo-superior-decide-dar-finalizado-torneo-clausura-2022|title=Consejo Superior decide dar por finalizado el Torneo Clausura 2022|trans-title=Higher Council decides to end the 2022 Torneo Clausura|language=Spanish|publisher=Los Tiempos|date=10 November 2022|access-date=10 November 2022}} [[Club Independiente Petrolero|Independiente Petrolero]] were the defending champions, having won the [[2021 FBF División Profesional|2021]] tournament. ==Format== The format for the 2022 season was approved by the 16 División Profesional clubs on 21 December 2021. The league returned to the [[Apertura and Clausura]] format after the year-long tournament held in [[2021 Bolivian Primera División|2021]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia|COVID-19 pandemic]]. The Torneo Apertura, which was played from 6 February to 12 June, had a first stage with the 16 participating clubs divided into two groups of eight, from which the top four clubs of each group advanced to a knockout stage in which the champions were decided. Meanwhile, the Torneo Clausura, played from 1 July to 10 November, was played under a double round-robin format.{{cite web |url=https://premiumsportsbo.com/tres-torneos-en-2022-el-apertura-por-series-empezara-el-6-de-febrero/|title=Tres torneos en 2022: el Apertura por series empezará el 6 de febrero|trans-title=Three tournaments in 2022: the Apertura by series will start on 6 February|language=es|publisher=Premium|date=22 December 2021|access-date=25 December 2021}}{{cite web |url=https://eldeber.com.bo/futbol/oriente-visitara-al-tigre-y-blooming-sera-local-ante-bolivar-en-la-primera-fecha-del-torneo-apertura_263225|title=Oriente visitará al Tigre y Blooming será local ante Bolívar en la primera fecha del torneo Apertura|trans-title=Oriente will visit the ''Tigre'' and Blooming will host Bolívar on the first matchday of the Apertura tournament|language=es|publisher=El Deber|date=11 January 2022|access-date=12 January 2022}} The distribution of international berths was confirmed on 11 January 2022. The champions of both tournaments, as well as the Torneo Clausura runners-up and the best placed team in the aggregate table would qualify for the [[2023 Copa Libertadores]], while the Torneo Apertura runners-up, the [[2022 Copa Bolivia|Copa Bolivia]] champions, and the next two best placed teams in the aggregate table would qualify for the [[2023 Copa Sudamericana]].{{cite web |url=https://eldeber.com.bo/futbol/conozca-los-premios-que-se-distribuiran-en-los-torneos-apertura-clausura-y-copa-bolivia_263185|title=Conozca los premios que se distribuirán en los torneos Apertura, Clausura y Copa Bolivia|trans-title=Get to know the prizes that will be distributed in the Apertura, Clausura, and Copa Bolivia tournaments|language=es|publisher=El Deber|date=11 January 2022|access-date=11 January 2022}} ==Teams== 16 teams competed in the league for the 2022 season, 14 of which took part in 2021. The 2021 [[Copa Simón Bolívar (Bolivia)|Copa Simón Bolívar]] champions [[F.C. Universitario de Vinto|Universitario de Vinto]] and the winners of the [[2021 Bolivian Primera División#Relegation/promotion play-off|promotion/relegation play-off]] [[Universitario de Sucre]], were both promoted for this season. The former competed in the top tier for the first time ever, while the latter returned after a 3-year absence.{{cite web |url=https://www.americatv.com.pe/deportes/futbol-mundial/universitario-vinto-ascendio-primera-division-bolivia-n423216|title=Universitario de Vinto ascendió a la Primera División de Bolivia|trans-title=Universitario de Vinto were promoted to the Bolivian Primera División|language=es|publisher=América TV|date=13 December 2021|access-date=25 December 2021}}{{cite web |url=https://www.lostiempos.com/deportes/futbol/20211220/desata-locura-sucre-real-regresa-afp|title=La "U" desata la locura en Sucre; Real regresa a la AFP|trans-title=The "U" triggers madness in Sucre; Real returns to the AFP|language=es|publisher=Los Tiempos|date=20 December 2021|access-date=25 December 2021}} The promoted teams replaced [[Club Real Potosí|Real Potosí]] and [[Club San José|San José]], who were relegated at the end of the previous season. ===Stadia and locations=== {{location map+ |Bolivia |float=right |width=400 |caption=Locations of the 2022 División Profesional teams. |places= {{location map~ |Bolivia |lat=-16.516667 |long=-68.166667 |label=
